children: The precious yellow metal steadied its fortunes as gold held steady after closing at its lowest level since September 2025. This comes as the market focuses on high inflation rates in the US and mounting losses on Wall Street.

On COMEX LIVE, the price of Gold stood at $3,856.40 per ounce compared to the previous close of 3,859.50. When it comes to Silver, the latest price stood at $46.940 per ounce compared to the previous close of $46.930 per ounce.
A Bloomberg report pointed out that traders have increased wagers that the Federal Reserve will tighten monetary policy further in 2027.

On Monday, Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said she supports modest, gradual rate increases, while noting that the central bank may need to consider larger moves if inflation worsens. Higher interest rates generally weigh on precious metals, which do not generate yields, the report further added.

Gold also faced pressure as Asian stocks were poised to follow US equities lower, with investors still cautious about the artificial intelligence trade. A recent sell-off in technology shares has prompted some traders to sell gold holdings to cover losses in other markets.

This week, investors will turn their attention to minutes from the US central bank’s October meeting. In comments on Monday outlining possible effects of AI, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh avoided direct remarks on monetary policy, consistent with his stated preference against offering short-term guidance on interest rates.

Another report, this time from Reuters, said Fed officials have continued to signal a hawkish approach. This report underscored remarks from Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid, who on Sunday said inflation remained too high and further efforts were required to ease price pressures. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly recently cited persistent services inflation in support of additional rate increases.
According to CME Group’s FedWatch tool, traders assign a 94% probability to a 25-basis-point rate hike next month and a 6% chance of a 50-basis-point increase.
Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, making it less attractive to investors.
Even as gold and silver steadied, platinum and palladium edged up. Meanwhile, the price of Brent crude, the global benchmark for crude oil, eased to $91.

title: Gold holds after hitting a near 14-month low as inflation pressure and AI worries persist
